raw:
[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "harvest < Old English hærfest “autumn; harvest-time” < Proto-Germanic *harbitaz / *harbistaz, related to the season of gathering",
    "reading": "The word names the season of gathering: the time when what was sown is reaped and brought in.",
    "languages": ["en", "ang"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary; Online Etymology Dictionary",
    "confidence": 0.98
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "har + vest; hear “har” as hard/harrow, vest as garment or remainder",
    "reading": "A hard covering: what is gathered is also what is clothed, wrapped, or vested for keeping.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.42
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "harvest ~ French “arrive-t-il?” by sound-play on har- / arri- and -vest / -vite; arrival of the gathered",
    "reading": "An arrival: the thing long awaited comes in at last, as if the field itself were saying “it arrives.”",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.18
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "HARVEST → VASTER H / HAT SERV / HEAR VTS (loose anagrammatic drift)",
    "reading": "Expansion after compression: what was hidden becomes vast, spread outward from a tight form.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.21
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "H A R V E S T = Hold And Reap, Value Extracted, Stored, Transformed",
    "reading": "A mnemonic of extraction: hold, reap, store, and transform the yield into use.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.12
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "H = two uprights joined; A = apex; V = vessel/opening; E = three bars; R = turning leg; S = serpent; T = crossbar",
    "reading": "An image of enclosure and crossing: the gathered thing is held between pillars, then turned, then sealed.",
    "languages": ["en", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.27
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "H(8)+A(1)+R(18)+V(22)+E(5)+S(19)+T(20)=93; 9+3=12; 1+2=3",
    "reading": "The sum resolves to three: a triadic completion, as if seed, growth, and gathering were one cycle.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.31
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "harvest and German Herbst “autumn” are cognate; the season itself is named by the gathering time",
    "reading": "Autumn is the gathered season: the year ripens into its own reaping.",
    "languages": ["en", "de"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary; Duden Herkunftswörterbuch",
    "confidence": 0.95
  }
]
